strings.name: Anders Hejlsberg
strings.role: Software engineer · Language and compiler designer
strings.summary: Raised in Denmark, Hejlsberg wrote early Pascal compilers and helped develop Turbo Pascal and Delphi at Borland. He joined Microsoft in 1996, helped design C# and later led TypeScript, adding type-checking tools for large JavaScript applications. His emphasis on fast feedback, compatibility and collaboration influenced successive development environments. These languages and compilers are products of sustained team and community work.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; reviewed November 15, 2026. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Helped design Turbo Pascal, C# and TypeScript, influencing modern programming-language tools and large-scale software development.

strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Studied engineering at the Technical University of Denmark without completing a degree.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Evolving development tools
strings.highlights.h1.text: Improved compilation and editing from Turbo Pascal to Delphi, shortening development feedback cycles.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Languages for larger systems
strings.highlights.h2.text: Helped design C# and led TypeScript, applying types and tooling to large software projects.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Reflecting on language and tool design
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed open development, compiler performance and AI coding’s tooling needs in a GitHub interview.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Public collaboration for TypeScript
strings.timeline.t2.text: The project moved to GitHub, deepening community participation through public issues and code review.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Announcing TypeScript
strings.timeline.t3.text: Introduced types and tools extending JavaScript for large application development.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Helping launch C#
strings.timeline.t4.text: Developed C# with Microsoft colleagues, combining type safety, object orientation and platform requirements.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joining Microsoft
strings.timeline.t5.text: Left Borland to work on languages and development platforms at Microsoft.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Launching Delphi
strings.timeline.t6.text: As a key architect, applied Pascal experience to visual application development tools.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Turbo Pascal appears
strings.timeline.t7.text: His compiler work became central to Borland’s product, emphasizing fast compilation and integration.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Born in Copenhagen
strings.timeline.t8.text: Raised in Denmark, later studied engineering and began developing microcomputer software.
